problem_statement: The stdio subsystem must provide a `stdio_notify` module with a function `stdio_set_notify(void (*cb)(void *arg), void *arg)` that registers a single callback to be invoked in ISR context whenever new data becomes available on stdin. The callback must be invoked by the active stdio backend when received input is placed into stdin, so an application thread that is sleeping on thread flags can wake when input arrives without blocking in `stdio_read()`. After such a wake-up, the thread must be able to drain and echo available stdin data, while still remaining able to wake from other events such as a timer. When no callback is registered, stdin handling must behave as before.

verification.reason: The problem statement clearly specifies the module name (stdio_notify), the public API (stdio_set_notify with its exact signature), the callback semantics (invoked in ISR context when data is placed into stdin, single callback, NULL disables), the backward-compatibility requirement (no callback = old behavior), and the expected use case (thread flags, draining stdin, coexisting with timer). The hidden tests exercise exactly these behaviors: registering the callback via stdio_set_notify, verifying that input triggers the callback (which sets a thread flag), echoing data via the existing stdio_read/stdio_available/stdio_write APIs, and confirming the timer still fires independently. All names and behaviors used by the test are either stated in the problem statement or are pre-existing repository symbols the agent can discover.
